## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Saṅgahitavāra* (Pvr 1.12) is an analytical section of the *Parivāra*, the final treatise of the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. As its title indicates, the text defines and categorizes which monastic rules or classes of offenses fall under the heading of or are subsumed by other rules [SuttaCentral]. A complete English translation of the section has been provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. None of the surveyed secondary literature passages discuss this specific text; occurrences of the word *saṅgahita* within the surveyed reference corpus instead reflect the generic grammatical participle meaning "included" or "encompassed" found across Sutta, Abhidhamma, and commentarial discussions.
Text-reuse calculations by DharmaNexus indicate that *Saṅgahitavāra* shares 140 textual units across 24 other Pali texts, predominantly within the *Parivāra* itself [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive alignments appear in the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4; 27 matching segments, sharing up to §1.2–1.3 with §45.5–45.6_1) and the *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11; 17 matching segments) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits substantial formulaic overlap with other categorical chapters of the *Parivāra*, such as *Saṅgahavāra* (Pvr 2.4 and Pvr 2.12), *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 1.16 and Pvr 1.8), and the homonymous *Saṅgahitavāra* (Pvr 1.4) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus reports any curated or machine-detected cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan Vinaya corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
